findings.title: $__range queries are no longer excluded from splitting
findings.body: The new `.map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...))` runs before the `partition(... , query => !querySupportsSplitting(query))` step. `querySupportsSplitting` relies on `isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr)` to keep queries that contain `$__range` out of the time-split batches (the existing comment even explains that splitting such queries is incorrect because `$__range` would then be resolved against a sub-range). Because `applyTemplateVariables` resolves template variables and global variables (including `$__range`/`$__range_s`/`$__from`/`$__to`) on the frontend with the FULL time range, the `$__range` token disappears from `expr` before the check runs. The `isQueryWithRangeVariable` predicate then returns false and the query gets partitioned into `normalQueries` and split into 1-day chunks, each chunk receiving the full range baked into the previously-interpolated `$__range`. The result is wrong data: e.g. `count_over_time({a="b"}[$__range])` over a 2-day dashboard range becomes `count_over_time({a="b"}[2d])` applied to a 1-day sub-range. The check needs to run on the original (pre-interpolation) expression, or `$__range` must be excluded from this frontend interpolation.

findings.title: Stale comment about $__range interpolation location
findings.body: The comment in `querySupportsSplitting` says `$__range` is "interpolated on the backend with the split timeRange". After this PR the variable is interpolated on the frontend (`datasource.applyTemplateVariables`) with the full timeRange before the splitting decision, so the justification given in the comment no longer matches the code path. If the exclusion is still intended, the comment should be updated to describe the new ordering (check pre-interpolation expr, or skip `$__range` in the interpolation step); otherwise the check should be removed entirely.

findings.title: Templates are interpolated once in runShardSplitQuery and again inside every nested runSplitQuery call
findings.body: `runShardSplitQuery` now calls `datasource.applyTemplateVariables` on every non-hidden, non-empty target and passes the interpolated list to `splitQueriesByStreamShard`. Each shard group later builds a `subRequest` from these already-interpolated targets and calls `runSplitQuery(datasource, subRequest, ...)`. Inside `runSplitQuery`, the new `.map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters))` re-runs template interpolation on the same queries. The test `'Interpolates queries before running'` codifies this by asserting `applyTemplateVariables` is called 5 times for a single-target request (1 + 4 shard groups). Beyond the wasted work, if `applyTemplateVariables` is not strictly idempotent (e.g. it touches scopedVars, fires telemetry, mutates caches, or escalates unknown variables to errors) the second pass can change behavior or throw. Either `runSplitQuery` should be told the targets are already interpolated (skip flag / do not re-apply), or `runShardSplitQuery` should defer interpolation to the inner `runSplitQuery` call.

findings.title: No regression test for $__range queries being excluded from splitting
findings.body: The new `'Interpolates queries before execution'` test only covers `$__auto` and `$step` interpolation. There is no test asserting that a query containing `$__range` (or `$__range_s`) is still routed into `nonSplittingQueries` and never time-split. Given that this PR moves the `querySupportsSplitting` decision to after interpolation, this is exactly the regression a test should pin down. Without it, the existing exclusion documented by the `querySupportsSplitting` comment can silently break (see the corresponding finding in `querySplitting.ts`).

findings.title: Assertion bakes in the redundant interpolation count
findings.body: The updated `'Interpolates queries before running'` test asserts `expect(datasource.applyTemplateVariables).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5)` for a single-target request, which is exactly the count produced by interpolating once in `runShardSplitQuery` and then once per nested `runSplitQuery` shard-group call (1 + 4). Hard-coding this number hides the redundant work (see finding in `shardQuerySplitting.ts`) and will need to be changed if/when the duplication is removed. A test that asserts the final `runQuery` payloads contain correctly interpolated `expr`/`step` (which it already does for the shard splitting test) is sufficient; asserting the call count of an internal helper locks in the current inefficiency and the $__range regression.
